ruleResults.detail: synthetic fixture; real deployment gates on subject request

flags.topic: Right to quiet enjoyment / notice of entry
flags.clauseExcerpt: The landlord may enter the premises at any time without notice to inspect or carry out works.
flags.citation: Rent Restriction / Landlord and Tenant Act (quiet enjoyment)
flags.explanation: A clause allowing entry at any time without notice conflicts with the tenant's right to quiet enjoyment; reasonable prior notice is generally required.

flags.clauseExcerpt: The tenant waives all rights to structural repair and accepts responsibility for all repairs including habitability.
flags.citation: Landlord and Tenant Act (implied covenant to repair)
flags.explanation: A landlord's duty to keep the premises habitable and structurally sound is typically not waivable by contract.

flags.clauseExcerpt: A late fee of 50% per day applies to any rent not received by the due date.
flags.explanation: A late fee that functions as a penalty rather than a genuine estimate of loss may be unenforceable. Interpretation varies.

flags.clauseExcerpt: The tenant shall pay a security deposit equal to six months rent.
flags.explanation: A deposit of several months' rent may exceed the statutory cap in some jurisdictions. Confirm the local limit.

flags.clauseExcerpt: The landlord may terminate the tenancy if the tenant makes a complaint to any authority.
flags.explanation: A clause permitting eviction in response to a tenant complaint may amount to unlawful retaliatory eviction.

fairness.disclaimer: These flags are candidates for human review, not legal advice. Each cites the governing law and is capped by an evidence class.
